title: Coherent shifts on a right Kan extension
statement: Let $D,L,D^{\prime}$ be categories with coherent integer shifts, as in [def-weil-triangulated-category], without requiring a triangulation. Let $Q:D\to L$ and $F:D\to D^{\prime}$ commute coherently with these shifts. Suppose $LF:L\to D^{\prime}$ and $\alpha:Q\circ LF\to F$ have the right Kan universal property: for every $G:L\to D^{\prime}$, composing a transformation $G\to LF$ with $\alpha$ after whiskering by $Q$ is a bijection onto the transformations $Q\circ G\to F$. Then $LF$ admits coherent integer-shift comparisons for which $\alpha$ commutes with shifts.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05SU (lemma-derived-shift), Lemma Tag 05SC (lemma-2-out-of-3-defined), Proposition Tag 05SE (proposition-derived-functor), LF part

proof.text: For each integer n, the source and target shift functors are equivalences. Precomposition and postcomposition by them transport terminal objects of right-extension categories. The shift comparisons of Q and F identify the corresponding extension problems. Apply the equivalence invariance and rightKanExtensionUniqueOfIso APIs of Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Basic.

The unique comparison between the two shifted Kan extensions gives shiftFunctor L n composed with LF isomorphic to LF composed with shiftFunctor D-prime n. Its defining counit equation is exactly the shift-compatibility square of alpha.

For zero, the unit comparison satisfies the counit equation. For a+b, the composite of the a and b comparisons satisfies it, using the coherence of Q and F. Right Kan hom-ext uniqueness identifies these candidates with the canonical comparisons. These are the two CommShift laws; the counit equations give NatTrans.CommShift alpha.
